s1.syndrome_frame: Painless swelling of the hard palate with slow and symmetrical growth
salient_findings: Painless swelling in the molar region of the hard palate
Swelling grew slowly and symmetrically over 10-12 weeks
Firm, elastic, non-ulcerated swelling on both sides of the hard palate
key_facts: 41-year-old man with no significant medical history
10-12 week history of painless swelling
Swelling located in the molar region of the hard palate
Swelling grew slowly and symmetrically
Denies dysphagia, odynophagia, or systemic symptoms
Family history is unremarkable
1.5 x 3.0 cm firm, elastic, non-ulcerated swelling on both sides of the hard palate
No cervical lymphadenopathy detected
Routine serum chemistry within normal limits
Serologies for hepatitis A, B, and C were negative
Palatal bone appeared uninvolved during excision
Wound healed slowly over 4-5 weeks

shortlist.label: Torus Palatinus
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of slow-growing, painless swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of firm, elastic swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Palatal Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Condition that can cause slow-growing, symmetrical swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that can cause a firm, elastic swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor that can cause a swelling on the hard palate, although less likely given the slow and symmetrical growth

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic Adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign salivary gland tumor that can cause a swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Granular Cell Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can cause a swelling on the hard palate, although less likely given the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant salivary gland tumor that can cause a swelling on the hard palate, although less likely given the slow and symmetrical growth

raw.rationale: The slow and symmetrical growth of the swelling, its location in the molar region of the hard palate, and the absence of ulceration or cervical lymphadenopathy are consistent with Torus Palatinus, a benign bony growth.

rejected.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: The absence of ulceration, systemic symptoms, and negative serologies for hepatitis make this less likely

rejected.label: Giant Cell Granuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with more rapid growth and may be associated with systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Palatal Fibromatosis
rejected.why: Usually presents with a more aggressive growth pattern and may be associated with cortical bone invasion

rejected.label: Fibroma
rejected.why: While possible, the bilateral and symmetrical nature of the swelling is more suggestive of Torus Palatinus

rejected.label: Pleomorphic Adenoma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a salivary gland tumor, often with a more rapid growth rate

rejected.label: Granular Cell Tumor
rejected.why: Often presents with a more rapid growth rate and may be associated with systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with more rapid growth, ulceration, and systemic symptoms
